page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor built on x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor. The system provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Hardware specifications include 64 GB of dedicated system memory, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Cache memory features 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core complex. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 variants such as VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and FMA.

The server includes no local disk storage, requiring external network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Network bandwidth is provisioned at a baseline of 20 Gbps, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. In synthetic benchmarks, single-core CPU execution places in the top 10% of tested instances, backed by top 25% performance in Geekbench single-core, multi-core, image processing, and text processing evaluations. Multi-threaded CPU execution and large-block memory bandwidth fall within the middle 50% benchmark tier.

The instance delivers strong single-threaded processing efficiency and memory performance relative to its hardware profile. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio prioritizes processor density over memory capacity, providing qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks that do not require high per-core RAM allocations. Tradeoffs include total reliance on network storage and standard multi-core scaling. Recommended workload fits include code compilation, image and text processing, web serving, and batch processing.

The instance lacks local storage, relying entirely on network volumes, and delivers a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. Benchmark results demonstrate top 10% single-core CPU performance alongside top 25% ranks in Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and text and image processing tests. Multi-core throughput and database operations score in the middle 50% tier. The compute-dense 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration delivers favorable cost efficiency for processor-heavy applications without high memory overhead. Workload fit includes software compilation, web serving, text and image processing, and compute-bound application servers.
